svg.aria-label: virtual-patch-copilot — from a finding to a live F5 band-aid to the code fix
svg.title: virtual-patch-copilot — from a finding to a live F5 band-aid to the code fix
svg.desc: Scan inputs feed eight agents. The agents find and verify a vulnerability, pick the strongest control, write the band-aid policy and prove it blocks the real exploit. The band-aid applies to F5 Distributed Cloud, F5 WAF for NGINX, or BIG-IP Advanced WAF in front of the untouched origin, and is retired once the code-fix PR merges.
svg.text: Find the vulnerability. Mitigate it live on the F5 proxy you already run.
Ship the code fix. Retire the band-aid.
read-only · a scan makes no cloud or repo writes
a human gate on every live change
one loop, one finding at a time
find — is it real, and what stops it?
each verified finding → the band-aid now, the code fix next
the policy didn't block → diagnose and retry until it does
a deterministic linter rejects a self-defeating policy before any live round-trip
model-independent — Claude, OpenAI, Gemini or local Ollama, chosen per agent in config/agents.yaml
one declarative band-aid, emitted for every enforcement point below
ENFORCE · THE F5 PROXY YOU ALREADY RUN
SaaS edge · the default target · all 7 controls
your own box · 3 forms, every one live-proven
waf, rate_limit, malicious_user, bot_defense — declined, each with its reason
your own appliance · 3 forms, every one live-proven
waf, rate_limit, malicious_user, bot_defense — declined, each with its reason
untouched — the attack is stopped in front of it
AFTER THE APPLY — THE BAND-AID IS TEMPORARY BY CONSTRUCTION
every mutating step is appended to an audit trail and exports as a
SHA-256-manifested evidence bundle for a change board.
